display_name: Lucia of Rome, companion of Rix

names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 6 iulie, «Sfânta Muceniță Lucia din Roma», with the rank words left off.

Read out of saint.gr's line for 6 Ιουλίου, «Άγιοι Λουκία η παρθενομάρτυς, Ρήξος βικάριος και πολλοί άλλοι που μαρτύρησαν στην Κομπανία», with the rank word left off; the page's own text writes it «Λούκια».

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 6. јул ст. ст., „Св. муч. Лукија“ — Св. is not a rank and муч. is the rank, which `types` already carries; both come off and the bare forename is left, which is all the heading gives. «of Rome, companion of Rix» in the display name is the corpus’s own disambiguation off two other books, and **this book calls that companion by another name entirely**, which is why none of it is built onto the form. `foldchk.py` returns NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM for «Лукија», so there is no fold.

The heading of days.pravoslavie.ru’s name page 2574, «Лукия Каппадокианка, Римская, дева, мц.», with the two rank words after the last comma left off — «дева» is the `virgin` the corpus’s `types` vocabulary carries. The epithet «Каппадокианка» is the page’s and is kept although the reading behind it makes her a native of Campania; the page is not corrected. `fk.mjs` returns no other holder.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 6 июля ст. ст. — «Мц. Лукии девы и с нею мчч. Рикса , Антония , Лукиана , Исидора , Диона , Диодора , Кутония , Ароноса (Ориона), Капика и Сатура (301).»

attestations.note: The day’s fifth entry, and its first name: the same menologion day this folder’s Romanian, Greek and Serbian rows already keep, the same companion Rix, the same martyrdom at Rome. The reading life4169 was opened and is fuller than either book the folder already rests on: she is a native of the Italian region of Campania, taken captive young by Rix, a chief of one of the German tribes, and carried abroad; he first pressed her to the pagan rites, then came to revere her and gave her and her maidservants a house of their own, and asked her prayers before his campaigns. After twenty years, hearing that Diocletian had raised a persecution, she asked leave to go back to Italy; Rix, by then a Christian himself, left his palace and family and went with her to Rome, where both were put to the sword by the sentence of the prefect Elius. The line closes «(301)», which is the year `rix-the-vicar` already carries and one year outside this folder’s «about 300» off the Охридски пролог. `dates` UNCHANGED and the conflict is in the report: unlike the Prologue’s 301 for Rix, this 301 is stated of the entry that names her first, which may be the witness the earlier reading wanted. This book calls her companion «Рикс (Авций)», which is the Αύκειος the Prologue made an emperor of, and so joins the two readings the folder’s own note left unjoined — but it calls him a «царь», a king, where saint.gr makes him a vicar, and no `types` were changed on either folder for that. ELEVEN NAMES ON THE RUSSIAN LINE AGAINST FIFTEEN ON THE GREEK, AND THE TWO LISTS ARE READ AGAINST EACH OTHER NAME BY NAME. The corpus already keeps this company off saint.gr’s «Άγιοι Εικοσιτέσσερις Μάρτυρες» of the same menologion 6/7 and the same year 301, which enumerates fifteen and then says «και άλλοι εννέα», and nine others. The Russian line names Lucia, Rix and nine more. Eight of those nine answer to a Greek name of the fifteen and take that folder’s russian row; the ninth, Исидор, is a name the Greek list does not print and is a new folder, `isidore-companion-of-lucia`. The alignment is positional as well as onomastic: Greek «… Κοττύιος. Όρωνος, Παπικός, Σάτυρος» against Russian «… Кутония , Ароноса (Ориона), Капика и Сатура» is four consecutive names in the same order. The seven Greek names the Russian line does NOT print — Ανατολίας, Άπαμος, Απολλώνιος, Νέας, Παππιανός, Σερίνος, Βίκτωρ — keep their undocumented russian rows and were left exactly as they stand. `dates` UNCHANGED: this line’s 301 is the year the folder already carries. The reading life4169 was opened; it is one account for the whole company and names the nine only in the closing sentence. No hymn on the day page stands under any of these names.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 6 iulie — «Sfânta Muceniță Lucia din Roma»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 6ης Ιουλίου — «Άγιοι Λουκία η παρθενομάρτυς, Ρήξος βικάριος και πολλοί άλλοι που μαρτύρησαν στην Κομπανία»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 6 Ιουλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and it is plainly the same woman — seized by Rix the vicar, bringing him to the faith, martyred with him in Campania. It heads them both «(; - 301)», a year the folder has no `dates` for and which is therefore reported and not written. The man the folder is named after has no folder of his own and is drafted as `rix-the-vicar`, and the «πολλοί άλλοι» of the line are the Twenty-four Martyrs of the same day's separate entry. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 19.07.2026 (6. јул ст. ст.) — „Св. муч. Лукија“

attestations.note: The day’s fourth entry, five sentences long. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, as every heading of this wave is — and this day one of them ends in a comma, which is kept. The Julian 6 July is the same menologion number this folder’s Romanian and Greek rows carry, so there is no second day and no §4 note is owed. **THE FIRST DATE OF ANY KIND THIS FOLDER HAS HELD.** `dates` was **null**: neither doxologia nor saint.gr gave her a year, though saint.gr gives her companion one. This book ends „Најзад заједно с царем пострада за Христа у Риму око 300 године“ — at last, together with the emperor, she suffered for Christ at Rome about the year 300. `death` 300 to 300, display «about 300», basis traditional, with „око“ quoted in the note, which is the shape this corpus already uses for an approximated year — `marius-of-persia` carries «c. 270» the same way. **AND THE YEAR ON THE OTHER FOLDER IS NOT USED.** `rix-the-vicar` holds `death` 301 off saint.gr, «Αγιος Ρηξος Βικαριος Που Μαρτυρησε Στην Κομπανια (; - 301)», and the page of the Twenty-four Martyrs beheaded with him says they suffered in 301. **That year is another folder’s and this folder’s date is not widened on it**, which is the standing prohibition; it is recorded here and left there. **THE COMPANION HAS A DIFFERENT NAME AND A DIFFERENT RANK IN THIS BOOK, AND NO IDENTIFICATION IS MADE.** This folder’s display name is «Lucia of Rome, companion of Rix», and `rix-the-vicar` is a **vicar** in Campania. This book says „У Кампанији зароби је варварски цар Авције“ — in Campania a **barbarian emperor Auceius** took her captive — and then that she converted him, and that she suffered together with him at Rome. Same province, same companion in the martyrdom, **and neither the name nor the rank matches**: Авције against Rix, a barbarian king against a vicar. **No identification is made and no row is added**; the `rix-the-vicar` row the folder already carries comes off another book and is not mine to remove, and the new prose names the man as this book names him, so that the reader sees two books and not one. `ls saints | grep -i auce` and `grep -ril Авције saints/` hold nobody. WHAT ELSE IS NEW, WHICH IS THE WHOLE OF HER STORY, THE FOLDER HAVING HELD NONE OF IT. That he wished to live with her and she resisted; that he then left her in peace to pursue her ascesis; **that she converted the emperor to the faith after he gained a victory in war through her prayer**; and that at the last they suffered together at Rome. `types` UNTOUCHED: `martyr` is there and „Св. муч.“ is the `martyr`. **`virgin` is refused**: her resisting him stands in the body, the heading carries no such word, and the entry says nothing about a vow. No `office`, no `locations`: Campania and Rome in a narrative are not coordinates, and a folder with a `locations` whose dates read as one year would still have to answer `map-span`. **NO NEW ROWS.** The folder relates `rix-the-vicar` already and this book gives that companion another name; the war and the victory are not folders. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse. **THE DAY’S THIRD ENTRY IS A FEAST AND IS REFUSED TWICE OVER.** „Обретеније моштију св. Јулијаније девице“ — the finding of the relics of the holy virgin Juliana. §5 is explicit that an «Обретење моштију» is a feast and not a folder, which is the first refusal; **and no folder holds her**, which is the second. The entry says she was the daughter of the prince of Olshansk, died about 1540 a virgin of sixteen, and that two hundred years after her death the diggers of a new grave beside the great church of the Kyiv lavra came on her relics whole and incorrupt, as though she had only just fallen asleep; many wonders came of them, and she herself appeared more than once to individual persons. `ls saints | grep -i juliana` returns seven and **not one of them is she**: `juliana-4-december`, `juliana-mother-of-saturninus`, `juliana-of-amisos`, `juliana-of-lazarevo`, `juliana-of-nicomedia`, `juliana-of-ptolemais` and `juliana-of-rhosus`. `ls saints | grep -i olshan` holds nobody. `foldchk.py` returns NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM for «Јулијанија». Ruling 3: named here, left out of every life written on this day, and no folder from me — and **the year 1540, the sixteen years, and the two hundred years are written nowhere**, the first being hedged „около“ in any case and the other two being durations. **AND THE ONE MAN IN THAT ENTRY WHO DOES HAVE A FOLDER TAKES NO ROW.** „знаменити Петар Могила“ — the famous Peter Mohyla — had one of those visions of her, and `peter-mohyla` is a folder kept venerated by the Romanian calendar on 22 December. An appearance is not a relation, which is the Three Hierarchs ruling; the entry is a feast, so no row of any kind hangs on it; and the folder it would hang on is Juliana’s, which does not exist.

death.note: The folder’s first date of any kind; `dates` was null before this reading, neither doxologia nor saint.gr giving her a year. The Охридски пролог for 6. јул ст. ст.: „Најзад заједно с царем пострада за Христа у Риму око 300 године“ — at last, together with the emperor, she suffered for Christ at Rome about the year 300. The book’s own „око“, about, is kept in the display. `rix-the-vicar`, whom this corpus names her companion, holds `death` 301 off saint.gr’s head line and off the page of the Twenty-four Martyrs beheaded with him; **that year is another folder’s and this field is not widened on it**. This book calls her companion a barbarian emperor Auceius rather than a vicar Rix, and no identification is made (5 October 2026).
